newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Dec 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Dec 4.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Relatives of one of the six men killed by police in the Suphan Buri province massacre have filed a complaint with the attorney-general. They insist the six were not amphetamine traffickers as alleged. (BANGKOK POST)

- House Speaker Wan Mohammad Noor Matha has said that he will not immediately resign to protest at the prime minister's failure to give his group a Cabinet seat, but has not ruled out quitting after the government announces its policy. His statement has refuelled tension within the New Aspiration Party after Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh had seemed to placate the southern faction with a promise to allocate a Cabinet seat in the next Cabinet reshuffle. (THE NATION) (BANGKOK POST)

- Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh plans to set up a community police force comprised of military and police personnel to tackle social woes. Chavalit, former Army chief, says this should be established as the 10,000-strong Metropolitan police force could no longer maintain law and order effectively. (THE NATION) (BANGKOK POST)

- In a flurry of image-making activity designed to win back some confidence in the Thai government's ability to manage the economy, Deputy Premier and Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan has invited International Monetary Fund managing director Michael Camdesus to visit Thailand on Dec. 10, at which time he will hold talks with PM Chavalit Yongchaiyudh. Camdesus has accepted the invitation. (THE NATION)

- Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan has confirmed that he would not become Chairman of the Securities and Exchange Commission to ensure that the regulatory agency experiences no political interference. Amnuay says he will select the appropiate outside specialist to take the chair in place of him. He will be the first finance minister not to take the position. (BUSINESS DAY)

- The Bank of Thailand's Rehabilitation Fund may reject Sitca Investment and Securities' demands and take over the ailing Bangkok Bank of Commerce (BBC) itself if no other party is interested in rehabilitating the troubled institution. Sitca is the only group of three applicants to qualify for the right to rescue the BBC. (BUSINESS DAY)
